# macdoc

> A safe, local-first macOS CLI that explains why a developer Mac is full and slow, and gets space back without surprises.

macdoc scans your Mac, shows where space and memory go, and suggests cleanups from a fixed recipe catalog. It deletes nothing by itself: a person approves each removal at a real terminal.

## Commands

Read-only (safe to run any time):
- `macdoc` (overview when piped), `macdoc scan`, `macdoc reclaim [toolchain] [--toolchains] [--categories]` (read-only without a terminal; at a real terminal it asks which risk types to clean (tick the boxes, then Enter on the Clean button; a typed answer of Enter alone is SAFE only; RISKY keeps apply's confirmations), which agents must never answer; it never offers an installed app, that is `retire`), `macdoc retire`, `macdoc refresh` (listing only), `macdoc explore [path] [--growth] [--projects]`, `macdoc vitals [--memory]`, `macdoc log`
- Every command supports `--json` (schemas in `schema/`).

Plans and removal (Terminal, person only):
- `macdoc apply --dry-run <O-ids>` seals a dry-run plan from opportunity IDs (never paths). It changes nothing.
- `macdoc apply` remains for specific IDs, other tiers and sealed or Claude-proposed plans.
- `macdoc apply <O-ids|--safe|--tier T|--recipe R|P-id>` seals a plan, shows the dry run and asks per item before removing. There is no `--yes`. Agents must not run it, except with `--dry-run` on request.
- `macdoc quarantine restore|purge` also belong to the person.

## MCP server

`macdoc mcp` lets an AI assistant diagnose and propose plans. It cannot apply, delete, move, restore, accept a path or run a command. The person runs the returned `macdoc apply P-...` in Terminal.
